answer_text:
Let

\[
g(z)=f(z)-\left(1+iz-z^3\right).
\]

Since \(f\) is entire, \(g\) is entire. For every positive integer \(n\),

\[
g\left(\frac1n\right)
=f\left(\frac1n\right)-\left(1+\frac{i}{n}-\frac1{n^3}\right)
=0.
\]

Also,

\[
g(0)=f(0)-(1+0-0)=1-1=0.
\]

Thus \(g\) has zeros at \(z=0\) and at \(z=\frac1n\to 0\). Since the zeros accumulate at a point in the domain and \(g\) is entire, the identity theorem gives

\[
g(z)\equiv 0.
\]

Therefore,

\[
f(z)=1+iz-z^3.
\]

Now evaluate at \(z=1-2i\):

\[
i(1-2i)=i-2i^2=2+i,
\]

and

\[
(1-2i)^2=-3-4i,
\]

so

\[
(1-2i)^3=(1-2i)(-3-4i)=-11+2i.
\]

Hence

\[
f(1-2i)=1+(2+i)-(-11+2i)=14-i.
\]

\[
\boxed{14-i}
\]
